ghow_default.document: Gerardi, Herkenhoff, Ohanian and Willen, Can't Pay or Won't Pay?
notes: An unemployed household head is about 5 percentage points more likely to default than an employed head.

A household in which BOTH head and spouse experience an unemployment spell is more than 8 percentage points more likely to default. This is the within-household correlated displacement factor the sudden-shock module needs, and it is SUPERADDITIVE: 8 against 5, not 10.
Job loss has an equivalent effect on default likelihood as a 35 percent decline in equity. That is the exchange rate between the two legs of the double trigger.
5 percent of the full sample is unemployed against 20 percent of defaulters.
